chunks: Muhammad ibn Sinan narrated from Ishaq ibn 'Ammar who said:

I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) say: 'Character (al-khalq) is a gift that Allah bestows upon whomever He wills from His creation. Some of it is a natural disposition (sajjiyyah) and some of it is acquired practice/intention (binyah). I asked: Which of the two is better? He said: The one with intention (niyyah) is better. For indeed, the one with natural disposition is compelled to act in that manner and cannot do otherwise, whereas the one with intention is the one who perseveres in obedience, so he is better.'

key_terms.بِنْيَةٌ: Acquired structure or practice based on intention

ai.seo_question: What is the difference between natural disposition and acquired character in Shia ethics?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) distinguishes between innate disposition (sajjiyyah), which is involuntary, and acquired character (binyah), which stems from conscious intention and effort. He asserts that the latter is superior because it involves voluntary perseverance in obedience to God, whereas the former is merely a compulsion of nature. This distinction highlights the Shia emphasis on *ikhtiyar* (free will) and the spiritual merit of striving against one's base nature to achieve higher moral states.
